content.text: The candidates belonging to the NRI/Non-Resident Indian category shall submit the following documents in original while reporting to the allotted college for admission. The NRI candidates must attend the document verification with the following certificates.

sections.heading: Additional Certificates Details

content.text: The following certificates are submitted only if the candidate belongs to that specific category. These categories are considered for reservation. Lack of valid documents or proof will make you considered as a general category candidate, and you will not be able to avail of the reservation benefits set by the government.
The following are the categories and the valid certificates and documents required for Ayush Counselling.
Disability Certificate

The candidates with benchmark disabilities belong under the category, and they must produce the Disability Certificate/ PwBD Certificate , one of the documents required for Ayush Counselling, authorized by the Medical Board for 21 Benchmark Disabilities as per the Rights of Persons with Disability Act, 2016.
An online generated PwBD certificate from the MCC portal will be issued by the designated disability centers. PwBD Certificate from any other hospital or organization will not be accepted.
Caste Certificate

The candidates under the SC/ST/OBC categories must submit relevant caste certificates issued by the competent authority. The students belonging to the SC/ST category need to submit the SC/ST Certificate , and the OBC category candidates must submit the OBC-NCL Certificate .
Income Certificate

The candidates of the general category, who fall under certain criteria of income, are eligible to apply under this category. And they must produce the GEN-EWS Certificate from a designated competent authority for the counselling.

sections.heading: Conclusion

content.text: The documents required for Ayush Counselling for the year 2025 are listed in the article. These documents play a vital role in the verification of the candidates during the counselling process. Thus, it is mandatory to submit all the original certificates for the document verification, and during the joining of the college, without fail, to ensure that there is no hindrance in the admission process. It is advisable to carry extra photocopies of the relevant original certificates to avoid any kind of inconvenience.

Disability Certificate

The candidates with benchmark disabilities belong under the category, and they must produce the Disability Certificate/ PwBD Certificate , one of the documents required for Ayush Counselling, authorized by the Medical Board for 21 Benchmark Disabilities as per the Rights of Persons with Disability Act, 2016.

An online generated PwBD certificate from the MCC portal will be issued by the designated disability centers. PwBD Certificate from any other hospital or organization will not be accepted.

Caste Certificate

The candidates under the SC/ST/OBC categories must submit relevant caste certificates issued by the competent authority. The students belonging to the SC/ST category need to submit the SC/ST Certificate , and the OBC category candidates must submit the OBC-NCL Certificate .

Income Certificate

The candidates of the general category, who fall under certain criteria of income, are eligible to apply under this category. And they must produce the GEN-EWS Certificate from a designated competent authority for the counselling.

Conclusion

The documents required for Ayush Counselling for the year 2025 are listed in the article. These documents play a vital role in the verification of the candidates during the counselling process. Thus, it is mandatory to submit all the original certificates for the document verification, and during the joining of the college, without fail, to ensure that there is no hindrance in the admission process. It is advisable to carry extra photocopies of the relevant original certificates to avoid any kind of inconvenience.

sections.heading: Gujarat Ayush Counselling Overview

content.text: Gujarat Ayush Counselling is supervised by the Admission Committee for Professional Undergraduate Medical Courses (ACPUGMEC) . For participating in the counselling, the eligible candidates need to register with the Gujarat Ayush Counselling official website at https://www.medadmgujarat.org/. Admission to the Ayush courses is only based on the NEET-UG scores of the current year.

While Ayurveda, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha & Homeopathy are the Ayush courses, Gujarat offers only BAMS and BHMS colleges. There are a total of 48 BHMS and 44 BAMS colleges in Gujarat as per the year 2025, according to ACPUGMEC.

The majority of the seats in the state are reserved for students with Gujarat domicile, with 85% of the seats allocated under the State Quota. Students from other states can apply to the Self-Financed BAMS and BHMS colleges under the All India Quota (AIQ), which reserves 15% of seats. The AIQ seats for counselling are under the Ayush Admissions Central Counseling Committee (AACCC) .

Candidates have to purchase PIN through the official website, https://medadmgujarat.org/ug , by making payment of the registration fees.
After purchasing of PIN, Candidates should register by submitting the application form with all the accurate details.
Upload the original relevant documents and certificates to complete registration.
The candidates must produce the original certificates and documents for verification at the designated center.
The documents can be retained after verification along with the registration slip, which is necessary for further admission procedures.
ACPUGMEC will release the official merit list of all the eligible candidates on their website.
Choice filling round is initiated for each round of allotment.
Candidates can arrange the colleges list according to their preference during choice filling. It is mandatory to lock the choices after each choice filling.
Allotment is made in 4 rounds: Round 1/ Round 2/ Round 3/ Stray Vacancy Round
Stray Vacancy Round is only for the vacant seats after all 3 rounds.
Seats are allotted considering NEET scores, merit rank, reservation criteria, and choices of colleges
The Allotment List is published on the official website of ACPUGMEC. Candidates can log in with their credentials to view the result.
After the list is published, candidates should obtain the Provisional Allotment Order.
The candidates should pay the prescribed tuition fees to the allotted college by cash/DD.
Candidates must report to the allotted college with all the necessary original documents, including the Provisional Allotment Order, and get them verified.

tables.section_heading: Gujarat Ayush Counselling Process- All India Quota

cells: NEET qualified Candidates should register with the official website of AACCC, www.aaccc.gov.in . Provide necessary personal information and submit the application form by making payment of the prescribed fee.Upload relevant original documents and certificates.

Candidates can fill in their preference for colleges in the option entry form, along with the state preference, Gujarat.Choice filling starts from the first round of allotment.It is mandatory to lock the choices after each choice-filling round.

Allotment is made to various institutions on the basis of NEET scores, merit rank, reservation, and choices of colleges.Allotment is processed in 4 rounds: Round 1/ Round 2/ Mop-up Round/ Stray Vacancy Round.The eligibility and participation rules for each round are different.

A final list of allotment is published on the official website of AACCC. Candidates can log in with their credentials to view the result.Candidates must download the Provisional Allotment Order after the publication of result.

The candidates should join the allotted college and produce the original certificates to them for verification.Make the payment of tuition fees prescribed by the allotted college to confirm admission.

Gujarat Ayush Counselling Overview

Gujarat Ayush Counselling is supervised by the Admission Committee for Professional Undergraduate Medical Courses (ACPUGMEC) . For participating in the counselling, the eligible candidates need to register with the Gujarat Ayush Counselling official website at https://www.medadmgujarat.org/. Admission to the Ayush courses is only based on the NEET-UG scores of the current year.

While Ayurveda, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha & Homeopathy are the Ayush courses, Gujarat offers only BAMS and BHMS colleges. There are a total of 48 BHMS and 44 BAMS colleges in Gujarat as per the year 2025, according to ACPUGMEC.

The majority of the seats in the state are reserved for students with Gujarat domicile, with 85% of the seats allocated under the State Quota. Students from other states can apply to the Self-Financed BAMS and BHMS colleges under the All India Quota (AIQ), which reserves 15% of seats. The AIQ seats for counselling are under the Ayush Admissions Central Counseling Committee (AACCC) .

Gujarat Ayush Counselling Eligibility Criteria

Below are the eligibility criteria for admission to Ayush courses. The candidates must strictly follow the requirements to participate in the Gujarat Ayush Counselling 2025.

Academic Qualification

The candidates should have passed in 10+2 and obtained a minimum aggregate of 50%, together in Physics, Chemistry, and Biology subjects, in the case of the general category, and 40% marks in the case of the reserved category (SC/ST/OBC).

Entrance Examination

NEET-UG qualification is mandatory for admission to Ayush courses. Candidates must obtain a minimum mark of the 50th percentile in the NEET examination.

In case of reserved category candidates (SC/ST/OBC), the minimum mark to obtain is the 40th percentile in the NEET examination.

Age Limit

The age of the candidates must not be less than 17 years on 31 December of the year of admission.

Domicile Requirement

The candidates who studied 10+2 in Gujarat can only apply to the private and government colleges under the Government and Management Quota.

The students with 10+2 from other states apart from Gujarat can apply for self-financed colleges under the 15% of AIQ seats.

Gujarat Ayush Counselling is conducted for admission to BAMS and BHMS colleges in the state. NEET-qualified students from Gujarat and other states can participate in the counselling.

Gujarat domicile candidates can participate in the counselling under the 85% seats of the State Quota

Other state students can participate in the Gujarat state counselling under the 15% seats of All India Quota (AIQ) conducted by the AACCC.

Gujarat state counselling for Ayush courses: BAMS/BNYS/BUMS/BSMS/BHMS are conducted by the Admission Committee for Professional Undergraduate Medical Courses (ACPUGMEC). NEET-UG qualified candidates can participate in the SKAU online counselling under either or both state quota and All India Quota, depending on the domicile of the candidate.

NEET-UG 2025 was held on 4 May 2025; NEET-G 2025 results were published on 14 June 2025. Haryana Ayush registration dates are yet to be announced officially.

Haryana Ayush Counselling Overview

Haryana Ayush Counselling is conducted by the Shri Krishna AYUSH University, Kurukshetra , for Ayurveda, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha & Homeopathy courses. Admission is offered to the BAMS and BHMS government/ government-aided/ private institutes, including those under private/ deemed universities in Haryana, recognized by the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) and National Commission for Homoeopathy (NCH).

https://skau.ac.in/ is the Haryana Ayush Counselling official website, where the candidates must register themselves to initiate the SKAU online counselling. NEET-UG qualification along with 10+2 higher secondary education in Physics, Chemistry, and Biology subjects is mandatory for Haryana Ayush Counselling.

The majority of Ayush seats in Haryana are reserved for domicile students under the State Quota of 85% seats. And the remaining 15% seats are open to all candidates, including non-domicile /non-resident candidates under the All India Quota (AIQ). All the seats counselling for AIQ under private and government colleges are conducted by the AACCC . There is 1 BHMS college and 15 BAMS colleges in Haryana participating in the Haryana Ayush Counselling 2025.

Haryana Ayush Counselling Process- State Quota

Here is the detailed procedure involved in the Haryana Ayush Counselling 2025 under the state quota.

Round 1

Registration and Fee Payment

Register for the Haryana Ayush Counselling through the official portal of Shri Krishna AYUSH University, Kurukshetra at skau.ac.in and fill out the application with necessary personal and academic details. Make payment of the registration fee as mentioned below.

Choice Filling & Locking

Fill in the choices of college in the option entry form according to your preferences and lock the choices before the last date.

Seat Allotment and Publication of Allotment List

Allotments are made based on the NEET rank of 2025, the reservation policy, and the choice of colleges. The allotment list is published on the official portal of the Haryana state counselling. Candidates must log in to the portal and download the provisional allotment letter.

Document Verification

Candidates must attend the document verification conducted by the concerned committee of the colleges with the original certificates and documents to get them verified.

Reporting to Allotted College

Allotted candidates must report to the college and produce the original documents, and make payment of the prescribed fees to the college to complete the admission process.

Round 2

Registration and Fee Payment

Register for the Haryana Ayush Counselling through the official portal of Shri Krishna AYUSH University, Kurukshetra at skau.ac.in for new candidates. Already registered candidates may not register again. The registration fee is the same as Round 1. Security fees for Round 2 are mentioned below.

Choice Filling & Locking

Fill in the choices of college in the option entry form according to your preferences and lock the choices before the last date. Fresh choices should be filled by all the candidates participating in Round 2.

Seat Allotment and Publication of Allotment List

Allotments are made based on the NEET rank of 2025, the reservation policy, and the choice of colleges. The allotment list is published on the official portal of the Haryana state counselling. Candidates must log in to the portal and download the provisional allotment letter.

Document Verification

Candidates must attend the document verification conducted by the concerned committee of the colleges with the original certificates and documents to get them verified.

Reporting to Allotted College

Allotted candidates must report to the college and produce the original documents, and make payment of the prescribed fees to the college to complete the admission process.

Mop-up Round

Registration and Fee Payment

Candidates who were not allotted seats, or did not join the allotted seats, or gave their willingness to upgrade seats in the Round 1 & Round 2 can participate in the Mop-up Round. Already registered candidates may not register again. The registration fee is the same as Round 1. Security fees for Round 2 are mentioned below.

Choice Filling & Locking

Fill in the choices of college in the option entry form according to your preferences and lock the choices before the last date. Fresh choices should be filled out by all the candidates

Seat Allotment and Publication of Allotment List

Allotments are made based on the NEET rank of 2025, the reservation policy, and the choice of colleges. The allotment list is published on the official portal of the Haryana state counselling. Candidates must log in to the portal and download the provisional allotment letter.

Document Verification

Candidates must attend the document verification conducted by the concerned committee of the colleges with the original certificates and documents to get them verified.

Reporting to Allotted College

Allotted candidates must report to the college and produce the original documents, and make payment of the prescribed fees to the college to complete the admission process.

Haryana Ayush Counselling Process- All India Quota (AIQ)

Here is the detailed procedure involved in the Haryana Ayush Counselling 2025 under the All India Quota (AIQ), conducted by the AACCC .

Registration and Fee Payment

Candidates must apply for the counselling through the official website of AACCC at aaccc.gov.in and submit the application by filling out the necessary information and uploading the relevant documents.

Make fee payment for counselling as prescribed by the AACCC according to your category.

Choice Filling/Locking

Candidates must fill out the choice of colleges during this round according to their preferences. It is mandatory to lock the choices after selection.

Seat Allotment

Allotment of seats is made according to the NEET scores, merit rank, reservation policy, and choice of colleges.

There are multiple rounds of allotment: Round 1/ Round 2/ Mop-up Round, and a stray vacancy round, if there are seats vacant after the previous rounds.

Publishing of Allotment List

The allotment list is published on the official website of AACCC. Log in to the website and download the allotment letter for further admission procedure.

Reporting to Allotted College

Candidates must report to the allotted college with the necessary original certificates for the document verification.

Make payment of the prescribed college fees to confirm your admission.

sections.heading: Jharkhand Ayush Counselling Overview

content.text: Jharkhand Combined Entrance Competitive Examination Board(JCECEB ) conducts the Jharkhand Ayush Counselling for Ayush Courses. To participate in the counselling, the eligible NEET-UG candidates must register with the Jharkhand Ayush Counselling official website at https://jceceb.jharkhand.gov.in/. Admission to the courses is solely based on the NEET-UG scores of the current year.

Ayurveda, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha & Homeopathy are the ayush courses, for which the counselling is undergone. However, Madhya Pradesh offers private and government homeopathy colleges recognized by the National Commission for Homeopathy for the Jharkhand counselling, as currently, there are no BAMS colleges in Jharkhand accepting students for the program through counselling.

Jharkhand reserves its 85% seats for domicile students of Madhya Pradesh under the State Quota. Students from other states/ non-domicile students can also apply to BHMS colleges in Jharkhand under the 15% seats of All India Quota (AIQ), conducted by the Ayush Admissions Central Counseling Committee ( AACCC).

sections.heading: Jharkhand Ayush Counselling Process

content.text: Jharkhand Ayush Counselling is carried out for admission to the BHMS colleges in Gujarat. NEET-UG qualified candidates can apply to the colleges through the Jharkhand counselling under different quotas.

items: Domicile students of Jharkhand can participate in the JCECEB counselling under the 85% seats of the state quota , reserved for them.
Non-domicile candidates/ students from other states can participate in the counselling under the 15% seats of All India Quota (AIQ), which is conducted by the AACCC .

sections.heading: Jharkhand Ayush Counselling Process- State Quota

content.text: Here is the step-by-step guide for the process involved in the Jharkhand Ayush Counselling under the state quota.

sections.heading: Registration

items: Visit the Jharkhand Ayush Counselling official website, https://jceceb.jharkhand.gov.in/, and fill out the application form with the necessary personal and academic details.
Upload photo, signature, and additional necessary documents as instructed.
Pay the registration/ counselling fees and submit the application form.

sections.heading: Publication of State Merit List

items: The merit list is published on the JCECEB website with the ranks according to your NEET-UG scores.

sections.heading: Choice Filling

items: Candidates must provide their preference for colleges during the choice filling session and lock their choices.

sections.heading: Seat Allotment

items: Seats are allotted to colleges based on the NEET rank of the candidates, the reservation policy, the choices of colleges, and the seat matrix of colleges.

sections.heading: Publication of Allotment List

items: The allotment results are published on the official website. Log in to the portal to view and download the Provisional Allotment Letter.

sections.heading: Document Verification and Admission

items: The candidates must attend the document verification at the designated center with the relevant original documents and get them verified.
Report to the allotted college, produce the original certificates, and make payment of the fees to complete the admission process.

sections.heading: Important Points to Note

items: The whole JCECEB Counselling process is carried out in multiple allotments (Round 1/ Round 2/ Round 3/ Stray Vacancy Round), with each round starting from registration to admission to the allotted college.

Candidates who are not allotted seats in any rounds, or did not join the allotted college, or gave their willingness to upgrade the seats, can participate in the subsequent rounds. Fresh candidates in each round have to register with fee payment for the allotment.
The Stray vacancy Round will be conducted for the vacant seats after allotment of the previous 3 rounds.
Fresh choices are filled in each round, and there are no restrictions on the number of preferences. Candidates can fill as many preferences as possible.

sections.heading: Jharkhand Ayush Counselling Process- All India Quota (AIQ)

content.text: Here is the step-by-step guide for the process involved in the Jharkhand Ayush Counselling under the All India quota (AIQ).

sections.heading: Registration & Fee Payment

items: Register with the official website of AACCC at aaccc.gov.in by providing the necessary personal and academic details and uploading the relevant certificates and documents.
Make payment of the counselling fee and register successfully.

sections.heading: Choice Filling/ Locking

items: During the choice filling session, candidates need to choose the state and colleges according to their preference. It is mandatory to lock the choices before the last date.

sections.heading: Seat Allotment

items: Seats are allotted in multiple rounds- Round 1/ Round 2/ Mop-Up Round/ Stray Vacancy Round.
In each round, participants need to register and fill in the choices of colleges. Already registered candidates any any rounds do not register again for the next round.
Allotment is made based on the NEET-UG score, reservation policy, seat availability, and choice of colleges by the candidates.

sections.heading: Publishing of Allotment Result

items: The Allotment Result is published on the official website of AACCC. Log in to the portal with your credentials and download the Allotment Letter.

sections.heading: Reporting to Allotted College

items: Candidates who are allotted seats must report to the respective college and submit the necessary original certificates and documents for verification.
Make payment of the prescribed college fee within the time frame provided to confirm seat at the college.

Jharkhand reserves its 85% seats for domicile students of Madhya Pradesh under the State Quota. Students from other states/ non-domicile students can also apply to BHMS colleges in Jharkhand under the 15% seats of All India Quota (AIQ), conducted by the Ayush Admissions Central Counseling Committee ( AACCC).

Jharkhand Ayush Counselling Dates

Jharkhand Ayush Counselling Fees

Jharkhand Ayush Counselling registration fees and counselling fees according to the category of the candidate are provided in the table below.

Jharkhand Ayush Counselling Eligibility

Refer to the criteria below to see whether you adhere to the eligibility requirements for Ayush courses in Jharkhand.

Academic Qualification

Candidates must have a 10+2 from a recognized board in 12th grade with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology as core subjects.

Candidates under the Unreserved category must obtain an aggregate score of 50% in the PCB subjects in their 12th grade.

Candidates under the reserved category must obtain an aggregate score of 40% in the PCB subjects in their 12th grade.

Qualifying Examination

NEET-UG qualification for the current academic year is mandatory for applying to counselling.

Age Limit

The candidate’s age must not be less than 17 years in the year of admission.

Domicile Requirement

Candidates must possess a valid domicile of Jharkhand to participate under the state quota. Non-domicile candidates are only eligible to participate under the AIQ.

Jharkhand Ayush Cutoff 2025

Cutoff is the minimum requirement for qualification for an examination that varies every year depending on certain factors. Jharkhand Ayush Cutoff is determined by the number of candidates who appeared and the difficulty level of the exam.

Ayush NEET Cutoff 2024

Documents Required for Jharkhand Ayush Counselling

Candidates are required to submit the original documents and certificates for document verification and at the allotted college for further admission formalities. The list of documents required for Jharkhand Ayush Counselling is provided in the table below.

Jharkhand Ayush Counselling Process

Jharkhand Ayush Counselling is carried out for admission to the BHMS colleges in Gujarat. NEET-UG qualified candidates can apply to the colleges through the Jharkhand counselling under different quotas.

Domicile students of Jharkhand can participate in the JCECEB counselling under the 85% seats of the state quota , reserved for them.

Non-domicile candidates/ students from other states can participate in the counselling under the 15% seats of All India Quota (AIQ), which is conducted by the AACCC .

Jharkhand Ayush Counselling Process- State Quota

Here is the step-by-step guide for the process involved in the Jharkhand Ayush Counselling under the state quota.

Registration

Visit the Jharkhand Ayush Counselling official website, https://jceceb.jharkhand.gov.in/, and fill out the application form with the necessary personal and academic details.

Upload photo, signature, and additional necessary documents as instructed.

Pay the registration/ counselling fees and submit the application form.

Publication of State Merit List

The merit list is published on the JCECEB website with the ranks according to your NEET-UG scores.

Choice Filling

Candidates must provide their preference for colleges during the choice filling session and lock their choices.

Seat Allotment

Seats are allotted to colleges based on the NEET rank of the candidates, the reservation policy, the choices of colleges, and the seat matrix of colleges.

Publication of Allotment List

The allotment results are published on the official website. Log in to the portal to view and download the Provisional Allotment Letter.

Document Verification and Admission

The candidates must attend the document verification at the designated center with the relevant original documents and get them verified.

Report to the allotted college, produce the original certificates, and make payment of the fees to complete the admission process.

Important Points to Note

The whole JCECEB Counselling process is carried out in multiple allotments (Round 1/ Round 2/ Round 3/ Stray Vacancy Round), with each round starting from registration to admission to the allotted college.

Candidates who are not allotted seats in any rounds, or did not join the allotted college, or gave their willingness to upgrade the seats, can participate in the subsequent rounds. Fresh candidates in each round have to register with fee payment for the allotment.

The Stray vacancy Round will be conducted for the vacant seats after allotment of the previous 3 rounds.

Fresh choices are filled in each round, and there are no restrictions on the number of preferences. Candidates can fill as many preferences as possible.

Jharkhand Ayush Counselling Process- All India Quota (AIQ)

Here is the step-by-step guide for the process involved in the Jharkhand Ayush Counselling under the All India quota (AIQ).

Registration & Fee Payment

Register with the official website of AACCC at aaccc.gov.in by providing the necessary personal and academic details and uploading the relevant certificates and documents.

Make payment of the counselling fee and register successfully.

Choice Filling/ Locking

During the choice filling session, candidates need to choose the state and colleges according to their preference. It is mandatory to lock the choices before the last date.

Seat Allotment

Seats are allotted in multiple rounds- Round 1/ Round 2/ Mop-Up Round/ Stray Vacancy Round.

In each round, participants need to register and fill in the choices of colleges. Already registered candidates any any rounds do not register again for the next round.

Allotment is made based on the NEET-UG score, reservation policy, seat availability, and choice of colleges by the candidates.

Publishing of Allotment Result

The Allotment Result is published on the official website of AACCC. Log in to the portal with your credentials and download the Allotment Letter.

Reporting to Allotted College

Candidates who are allotted seats must report to the respective college and submit the necessary original certificates and documents for verification.

Make payment of the prescribed college fee within the time frame provided to confirm seat at the college.

Conclusion

Jharkhand Ayush Counselling is the process of admission to Ayush courses such as BAMS/BNYS/BUMS/BSMS/BHMS. Jharkhand Combined Entrance Competitive Examination Board(JCECEB) is the state Ayush counselling conducting authority in Jharkhand. NEET-UG qualified candidates are only eligible to participate in the counselling. 6 BHMS colleges participate in the counselling offering seats under both state quota and All India Quota. The domicile students of Jharkhand can apply for 85% of the seats under the state quota. And the remaining 15% seats come under the All India Quota (AIQ), which is open to all categories.

KEA AYUSH Counselling comprises counselling of the 85% Ayush seats, reserved for the domicile students.

The remaining 15% are All India Quota seats handled by the AACCC. Non-Domicile students can apply for Karnataka colleges through AIQ quota under AACCC Counselling.

Karnataka accommodates 82 BAMS colleges , 18 BHMS colleges, 5 BUMS colleges, and 10 BNYS colleges, which include both private and government establishments. Admission to these colleges is only accepted through the Karnataka AYUSH counselling.

Karnataka Ayush Counselling Process 2025

Registration

Document Verification

After completing the registration, the necessary documents and certificates need to be uploaded as per the guidelines given. Option Entry

After document verification, the candidates will be given access to fill in their choices of college in the option entry form. Fill in the choices of colleges considering the eligibility and personal preferences.

Mock Allotment

Registration & Fee Payment

Processing of Seat Allotment

The candidates who surrender seats after the second round allotment, the entire fee paid will be forfeited.

sections.heading: Centralized Admission Process (CAP) & Online Submission of Options

items: The Centralized Admission Process (CAP) is conducted by the Commissioner of Entrance Examinations (CEE) for admission to Ayush Courses.

sections.heading: Registration and Fee Payment

items: The candidates should register with the website of cee.gov.in with the login id and password. Fill out the application form with basic personal details and make payment of the registration fees through the online payment gateway or e-chalan.

sections.heading: Document Verification

items: The candidates must attend the document verification procedure at the designated center with all the necessary original documents. After verification, the documents can be retained.

sections.heading: Choice Filling/ Locking

items: Upon the opening of the preference form, candidates must log in with their credentials and fill out their choices of colleges from the available options.
It is mandatory to lock the options before the final date to proceed to the allotment rounds.

sections.heading: Seat Allotment

items: Seat allotment is processed in multiple rounds. There is a total of 4 rounds: Round 1/Round 2/Round 3/Stray Vacancy Round.

Allotment is made under the State Merit Quota, irrespective of the reservation policy benefits. After all the State Merit Quota seats are filled, the remaining seats are allotted as per the respective reservation of the category, as per the reservation policy.
Stray Vacancy seats allotment is only made for the vacant seats. The candidates who did not secure seats in any of the previous rounds can participate in the Stray Vacancy Round.

sections.heading: Publication of Allotment List

items: The final allotment list will be published on the official website of CEE after considering the NEET scores, the reservation policy, choice options of the candidates.

sections.heading: Physical Reporting to the College

items: The candidates must join the college they are finally allotted and produce the necessary original certificates to process further admission.
They must pay the prescribed fees in the institution within the timeframe to confirm their seats.

sections.heading: Registration & Fee Payment

items: The counselling for All India Quota seats is carried out by the Ayush Admissions Central Counseling Committee (AACCC). The candidates must register with the official website of AACCC at aaccc.gov.in .
Log in using the ID and password to fill out the application form with personal information and make payment of the registration fee as prescribed according to the category.
Upload the necessary original documents and certificates.

sections.heading: Choice Filling/Locking

items: Choice filling round involves the candidates filling out their preferences for colleges in the option entry form. Fill in the choices by selecting the state Kerala, and choose colleges from the available list.
After filling in the options, choices must be locked before the last date to proceed to further rounds of counselling.

sections.heading: Processing of Allotment

items: The allotment will be held in a total of 4 rounds. The Stray Vacancy round is there for the remaining vacant seats after 3 rounds of allotment. Eligibility and participation for each round are different.

sections.heading: Publication of Allotment Results

items: After considering the NEET scores, choices of colleges, and reservation policy, seats are allotted, and the final Allotment List is published on the official website of AACCC.

sections.heading: Reporting to the Allotted College

items: The candidates allotted seats should report to the college with the necessary certificates for verification. The original certificates must be submitted to the college, photocopies will not be accepted.
Make payment of the prescribed fees to confirm the seat at the allotted college.

Kerala Ayush Counselling Process- State Quota

The following is the detailed procedure for Kerala Ayush Counselling 2025 under the State Quota.

Centralized Admission Process (CAP) & Online Submission of Options

The Centralized Admission Process (CAP) is conducted by the Commissioner of Entrance Examinations (CEE) for admission to Ayush Courses.

The candidates can register their options for courses and colleges through the CEE Kerala website. The options should be registered only if the candidates are willing to join if allotted.

Registration and Fee Payment

The candidates should register with the website of cee.gov.in with the login id and password. Fill out the application form with basic personal details and make payment of the registration fees through the online payment gateway or e-chalan.

Upload the necessary original documents and certificates as instructed.

Document Verification

The candidates must attend the document verification procedure at the designated center with all the necessary original documents. After verification, the documents can be retained.

Choice Filling/ Locking

Upon the opening of the preference form, candidates must log in with their credentials and fill out their choices of colleges from the available options.

It is mandatory to lock the options before the final date to proceed to the allotment rounds.

Seat Allotment

Seat allotment is processed in multiple rounds. There is a total of 4 rounds: Round 1/Round 2/Round 3/Stray Vacancy Round.

Allotment is made under the State Merit Quota, irrespective of the reservation policy benefits. After all the State Merit Quota seats are filled, the remaining seats are allotted as per the respective reservation of the category, as per the reservation policy.

Stray Vacancy seats allotment is only made for the vacant seats. The candidates who did not secure seats in any of the previous rounds can participate in the Stray Vacancy Round.

Publication of Allotment List

The final allotment list will be published on the official website of CEE after considering the NEET scores, the reservation policy, choice options of the candidates.

Physical Reporting to the College

The candidates must join the college they are finally allotted and produce the necessary original certificates to process further admission.

They must pay the prescribed fees in the institution within the timeframe to confirm their seats.

Kerala Ayush Counselling Process- All India Quota

The following is the detailed procedure for Kerala Ayush Counselling 2025 under the All India Quota.

Registration & Fee Payment

The counselling for All India Quota seats is carried out by the Ayush Admissions Central Counseling Committee (AACCC). The candidates must register with the official website of AACCC at aaccc.gov.in .

Log in using the ID and password to fill out the application form with personal information and make payment of the registration fee as prescribed according to the category.

Upload the necessary original documents and certificates.

Choice Filling/Locking

Choice filling round involves the candidates filling out their preferences for colleges in the option entry form. Fill in the choices by selecting the state Kerala, and choose colleges from the available list.

After filling in the options, choices must be locked before the last date to proceed to further rounds of counselling.

Processing of Allotment

The allotment will be held in a total of 4 rounds. The Stray Vacancy round is there for the remaining vacant seats after 3 rounds of allotment. Eligibility and participation for each round are different.

Publication of Allotment Results

After considering the NEET scores, choices of colleges, and reservation policy, seats are allotted, and the final Allotment List is published on the official website of AACCC.

Reporting to the Allotted College

The candidates allotted seats should report to the college with the necessary certificates for verification. The original certificates must be submitted to the college, photocopies will not be accepted.

Make payment of the prescribed fees to confirm the seat at the allotted college.

Rajasthan Ayush Counselling is conducted by the UG/PG Ayush Counselling Board, Govt. of Rajasthan , for admission to Ayush Courses: BAMS/BNYS/BUMS/BSMS/BHMS. The primary criterion for admission to the Ayush courses is the NEET-UG qualification. Seats are offered to all the Ayush colleges in the state, recognized by the NCISM and NCH under different quotas such as State Quota, All India Quota, and NRI Quota.

The NEET-UG 2025 examination was held on 4 May 2025, and the results were published on 14 June 2025. Rajasthan Ayush Counselling dates have not yet been officially published by the authorities.

This article will provide detailed insight into the Rajasthan Ayush Counselling 2025, including the counselling process, fees, cutoff, and more.

Rajasthan Ayush Counselling Overview

Rajasthan NEET Ayush UG/PG Counselling Board is in charge of conducting the UG counselling for Ayurveda, Naturopathy, Unani, Homeopathy, & Siddha courses. Candidates must register with the Rajasthan Ayush Counselling 2025 official website at rajugpgayushcounselling.in to apply to the Ayush colleges in Rajasthan. NEET-UG qualification of the current year is the mandatory requirement for participating in the counselling. BNYS is the only Ayush course that does not require NEET qualification for admission.

Rajasthan has 18 BAMS colleges , 12 BHMS colleges, 2 BUMS colleges, and 15 BNYS colleges participating in the state counselling. The state offers admission under the State Quota, All India Quota (AIQ), and NRI Quota. The 85% seats of the state are offered to the domicile students of Rajasthan under the state quota . The rest 15% seats are open to non-domicile students/ students from other states under the All India Quota(AIQ) for admission to private Ayush institutions. The 15% AIQ seats counselling for government colleges is conducted by the AACCC.

Rajasthan Ayush Counselling Process

Rajasthan Ayush Counselling Types

Rajasthan State Ayush Counselling offers seats in Ayush Colleges under different quotas: the State Quota, All India Quota (AIQ), and the NRI quota.

Rajasthan Ayush Counselling Process- State Quota

Round 1

Registration: The candidates must register with the Rajasthan Ayush Counselling official website at rajugpgayushcounselling.in and submit the application form along with the fee payment. The relevant documents should be uploaded to the website to complete the application.

Publication of Provisional List for Verification

Document Verification: Document verification is conducted by the Counselling Board for PwD, Defence Para-military, and NRI candidates. The candidates must submit the original documents for verification.

Publication of Provisional Merit List

Choice Filling & Locking: Candidates can fill in the choice of colleges according to their preferences and lock their choices. It is mandatory to pay INR 25,000/- counseling fees before choice filling. The fees paid will be considered part of the tuition fee later when joining the college.

Publication of First Round of Allotment Result: Allotment results are published based on the NEET scores, reservation policy, and choice of colleges.

Downloading of Allotment Letter: Candidates must log in to the Raj Ayush official portal and download the Provisional Allotment Letter.

Reporting cum Joining Allotted College: The candidates must report to the allotted college with original documents and complete the admission formalities, along with fee payment.

Round 2

Publication of Vacant seats for the 2nd Round.

Registration and Fee payment: The candidates newly registering must submit the application form, upload documents and make payment of fees. The candidates already registered in the Round 1 do not register again.

Choice Filling and Locking: All the candidates, including previously registered candidates can fill in the choice of colleges. It is mandatory to pay INR 25,000/- counseling fees before choice filling. The fees paid will be considered part of the tuition fee later when joining the college.

Publication of Seat Allotment Result: Allotment results are published based on the NEET scores, reservation policy, and choice of colleges.

Downloading of Allotment Letter: Candidates must log in to the Raj Ayush official portal and download the Provisional Allotment Letter.

Reporting cum Joining Allotted College: The candidates must report to the allotted college with original documents and complete the admission formalities, along with fee payment.

Mop-up Round

Publication of Vacant seats for the Mop-up Round

Choice Filling and locking (For new and previously registered candidates)

Rajasthan Ayush Counselling Process- All India Quota(AIQ)

Registration and Fee Payment: The candidates must register with the official website of AACCC at aaccc.gov.in . Upload the necessary documents and make the fee payment.

Choice Filling/Locking: Candidates can fill in the choice of colleges and state according to their preference, and later lock their choices.

Seat Allotment: Seats are allotted based on the NEET ranks, the seat matrix in the colleges, the choice of colleges, and the reservation criteria.

Publication of Provisional Allotement Letter: The provisional allotment letter is published on the official website of the college. Download the allotment letter for further admission process.

Physical Reporting to College: Candidates must report to the allotted college with the relevant documents and complete the admission procedure, including fee payment.

AIQ Counselling is conducted in 4 rounds, including Round 1/Round 2/ Mop-up Round/ Stray Vacancy Round. Check out the article on AACCC Ayush Counselling to learn more.

Conclusion

Rajasthan NEET Ayush UG/PG Counselling Board conducts the Rajasthan Ayush Counselling 2025 for admission to Ayurveda, Unani, Homeopathy, and Siddha UG Ayush Colleges in Rajasthan for BAMS/BUMS/BHMS/BNYS courses. The admission to the courses is solely based on the NEET ranks. The Rajasthan State Ayush Counselling is offered under the State Quota of 85% seats reserved for the domicile students of Rajasthan, All India Quota of 15% to private institutions in Rajasthan for non-domicile students, and NRI quota. The All India Quota seats of 15% to the government institutions are handled by the AACCC.

sections.heading: Ayush Counselling in Tamil Nadu Overview

content.text: Ayush Counselling in Tamil Nadu is conducted by the Directorate of Indian Medicine and Homeopathy, Chennai , for admission to Ayurveda, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha & Homeopathy courses in private and government colleges of Tamil Nadu. http://www.tnhealth.tn.gov.in is the official website for TN Ayush Counselling, where the candidates shall register themselves to apply to the Ayush colleges. The candidates who qualified the NEET-UG examination of the present academic year and have 10+2 with science stream and subjects, Physics, Chemistry, and Biology, are eligible to participate in the counselling.

The state counselling mainly reserves 85% of the seats for the domicile students of Tamil Nadu under the State Quota. The remaining 15% of seats are open to all candidates, including students from other states under the All India Quota (AIQ). Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling 2025 is the State Counselling procedure for admission to Ayush Courses: BAMS/BNYS/BUMS/BSMS/BHMS, supervised by the Directorate of Indian Medicine and Homeopathy, Chennai. The NEET examination qualification conducted by the NTA is the preliminary criterion for admission to these courses in Tamil Nadu. TN Ayush Counselling is conducted for seats in private and government colleges in the state, which are approved by the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) and the National Commission for Homeopathy (NCH) under both state and All India Quota.

The NEET-UG 2025 exam was held on 4 May 2025, and the results were out on 14 June 2025. The starting dates of TN Ayush Counselling are yet to be released.

This article will provide you with the complete information regarding the counselling procedure, including important dates, fees, and cutoff.

Ayush Counselling in Tamil Nadu Overview

Ayush Counselling in Tamil Nadu is conducted by the Directorate of Indian Medicine and Homeopathy, Chennai , for admission to Ayurveda, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha & Homeopathy courses in private and government colleges of Tamil Nadu. http://www.tnhealth.tn.gov.in is the official website for TN Ayush Counselling, where the candidates shall register themselves to apply to the Ayush colleges. The candidates who qualified the NEET-UG examination of the present academic year and have 10+2 with science stream and subjects, Physics, Chemistry, and Biology, are eligible to participate in the counselling.

The state counselling mainly reserves 85% of the seats for the domicile students of Tamil Nadu under the State Quota. The remaining 15% of seats are open to all candidates, including students from other states under the All India Quota (AIQ). The counselling for the AIQ seats to private and government colleges in Tamil Nadu is handled by the AACCC .

There are a total of 18 BAMS colleges , 18 BNYS colleges, 1 Unani college (BUMS), 15 Siddha colleges (BSMS), and 14 BHMS, Homeopathy colleges in Tamil Nadu, participating in the counselling.

Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling 2025 Highlights

Ayush Courses List

Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling 2025- Dates and Events

The table below outlines the dates and schedule for important events involved in Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling 2025.

Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling Registration Fees

Here are the category-wise fees to be paid for the application of Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling.

Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling Eligibility

The Eligibility requirements for participating in the Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling 2025 are mentioned below.

Entrance Examination:

NEET Qualification is mandatory for participating in the TN Ayush Counselling. The candidates belonging to the general category must obtain the 50th percentile, while the reserved category candidates must secure the 40th percentile in the qualifying examination.

Academic Qualification :

The candidates belonging to the general category must have passed the higher secondary examination with a minimum aggregate of 50% in the Physics, Biology, and Chemistry subjects.

The candidates belonging to the reserved category must have passed the higher secondary examination with a minimum aggregate of 50% in the Physics, Chemistry, and Biology subjects.

Age Limit:

The age of the candidates must be 17 or above in the year of admission.

Eligibility Certificate:

The candidates of other Universities / Boards (except State Board / CBSE / ICSE) have to submit the Eligibility Certificate obtained from the Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University, Chennai.

Domicile Requirement:

Candidates from other states will be considered in the open category.

Seat Reservation Policy

Allotment is made after considering the reservation policy for every category. Below is the seat reservation policy according to the category of the candidates.

Tamil Nadu Ayush Cutoff 2025

The cutoff score is the minimum score requirement for every year and is decided upon the difficulty level of the exam and the number of candidates who appeared. Here is the Ayush NEET cutoff 2025 for Ayush courses in Tamil Nadu.

Documents Required for Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling

The list of relevant documents and certificates is mentioned in the table below. The list includes the necessary original certificates to be sent along with the application form to the counselling authority. The original documents are to be submitted for document verification and to the allotted college upon joining. Carry 2 or 3 photocopies of the documents to avoid any kind of inconvenience in the admission process.

Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling Process- State Quota

Here’s the detailed procedure for Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling for applying to the state quota.

Registration & Fee Payment

The NEET qualified candidates must register themselves with the official website of the state counselling authority at www.tnhealth.tn.gov.in and fill out the application form with necessary personal and academic details.

Download the application form and, along with the relevant document, send it to the concerned authority.

Make payment of the application fee according to the respective category of the candidates to confirm registration.

Document Verification

Attend the document verification process at the designated centers with the original certificates. They can be retrieved after the verification.

Choice Filling/ Locking

Log in to the official website with your credentials and fill in the choices of colleges in the option entry form.

Arrange the list of colleges according to your preference.

It is mandatory to lock the choices before the last date.

Seat Allotment

Seat allotment is made in multiple rounds, including a mop-up round and a stray vacancy round.

The Stray Vacancy round is conducted only for the vacant seats that remain after the previous rounds of allotment.

Publication of Allotment Results

The results of the allotment are published on the official website. Log in with your credentials to access the list.

Allotment of seats is made on the basis of the NEET scores, Merit rank, Reservation policy, and the Choices of Colleges.

Download the allotment letter if you are allotted to a college.

Reporting to the College

After the allotment results are published, the candidates should join the allotted college within the time frame specified.

Carry the original documents and certificates along with the Allotment letter to the college for verification.

Complete the admission formalities and confirm seat at the college by making payment of the college fees.

Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling Process- All India Quota

The All India Quota seats counselling is conducted by the Ayush Admissions Central Counseling Committee (AACCC) . The candidates should register themselves with the official website of AACCC at aaccc.gov.in for the counselling.

The candidates can directly apply through the Directorate of Indian Medicine and Homeopathy (DIMH), Tamil Nadu, for self-financing colleges by downloading the application form from the website of www.tnhealth.tn.gov.in.

Here is the detailed procedure for applying under the India Quota (AIQ) for Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling.

Registration & Fee payment

Visit the official website of AACCC at https://aaccc.gov.in/ and click on the registration link.

Fill out the application form with personal details. Incorrect information may affect the eligibility of the candidate.

Make payment of the registration fees as prescribed for the respective category.

Upload scanned original documents and certificates to complete the registration.

Choice Filling/ Locking

Choice filling round enables the candidates to fill out the options entry form with the list of preferred colleges and the state.

Candidates can select Tamil Nadu state and arrange the colleges in the list according to their preference.

It is mandatory to lock the choices within the specified deadline.

Processing of Seat Allotment

The allotment process involves multiple rounds: Round 1/Round 2/Mop-up Round/Stray Vacancy Round.

The rules and participation for every round are different.

Seats are allotted on the basis of merit rank, NEET scores, reservation policy, and choices of colleges.

Publication of Allotment List

Provisional and final lists of Allotment are published on the official website of AACCC.

Log in to the portal with your credentials and download the allotment letter if you are allotted a college.

Reporting to the Allotted College

The candidates who are allotted colleges must report to the respective college within the time frame provided.

Carry the relevant original documents and certificates for verification at the college.

Complete the admission procedure with payment of the college fees within the prescribed time.

Check out the article on NEET Ayush Counselling 2025 to learn the complete information on the AIQ counselling process.

Conclusion

The Directorate of Indian Medicine and Homeopathy, Chennai, is the state counselling authority in Tamil Nadu for admission to Ayush courses such as BAMS, BNYS, BUMS, BSMS, and BHMS. The private and government colleges recognized by the NCISM, NCH, and the Ministry of Ayush participate in the counselling. Domicile students can apply under the 85% seats of the State Quota, and students from other states can apply for 15% of the seats under the AIQ through AACCC. It is mandatory for candidates to have higher secondary education with the minimum prescribed percentage in Physics, Chemistry, and Biology, along with the NEET-UG qualification, to be eligible for TN Ayush Counselling.

For regular updates on Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling or any other state Ayush Counselling 2025, follow our series of Ayush Counselling articles. Both private and government Ayurveda, Homeopathy, and Unani institutions, recognized by the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) and National Commission for Homeopathy (NCH), participate in the counselling. There are 80 BAMS colleges , 13 BHMS colleges, and 13 BUMS colleges in the state.

The NEET-UG examination conducted by the NTA serves as the primary criterion for admission to the Ayush courses. The NEET-UG qualified candidates with an academic background of higher secondary education in the science stream must register with the UP Ayush Counselling official website at https://upayushcounseling.upsdc.gov.in/ to participate in the counselling.

The State reserves 85% of the seats under the State Quota only for the domicile students of Uttar Pradesh, and the remaining 15% seats are under the All India Quota (AIQ) , open to all candidates, including non-domicile/ students from other states.

content.text: The Bachelor’s of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery is a five and a half year undergraduate course. It helps the students to combine traditional Ayurvedic medicine with modern medical practices. The eligibility for the BAMS course requires the candidate to qualify for the NEET exam. Three colleges provide BAMS admission in Andhra Pradesh. One of them is a government college, and the other two are private. The Government college holds 75 seats for BAMS admission every year, and the private ones have 90 seats each. In this article, we will cover the important details regarding BAMS admission in Andhra Pradesh, including the list of colleges, their eligibility, and fees.

sections.heading: How to Take BAMS Admission in Andhra Pradesh

content.text: For BAMS admission in India , colleges solicit students who are eligible for BAMS admission via the NEET merit. NCISM, New Delhi, Ministry of Ayush, has stated that there shall not be any offline admission or admission without counselling (Central/State/UT). And any admissions in contravention of this shall not be approved. Hence, all admissions under Management will be conducted by Dr. NTR UHS, Vijayawada , only(They are the only counselling authority for Andhra Pradesh Ayush Counselling ). In total, there are 255 seats available for BAMS admission in Andhra Pradesh.

sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria for BAMS Admission in Andhra Pradesh

content.text: In the state of Andhra Pradesh, the eligibility criteria for BAMS admission are pretty much the same as in any other state in the country. BAMS eligibility in Andhra Pradesh requires the students to pass NEET with a minimum required marks and attend the AYUSH state counselling process to book seats at their desired colleges. The eligibility guidelines are as follows.
Entrance Exam: The National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET UG)
Academic Qualification:

items: Candidates need to score a minimum of 50% aggregate in the Physics, Chemistry, and Biology subjects in their 12th examination. There is a relaxation of aggregate marks for the reserved candidates (Minimum 40% aggregate for SC/ST students)
Students must pass the 10+2 board examination from a recognised board.
Students should have passed the science stream with subjects Physics, Chemistry, and Biology/Biochemistry.

content.text: Age Limit: Candidates should have completed the age of 17 years as on the 31st December of the previous year.

sections.heading: BAMS Admission Process in Andhra Pradesh

content.text: Dr. NTR University of Health Science oversees the whole procedure for BAMS admission in Andhra Pradesh. The National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) and the Ministry of AYUSH made a statement that no offline admission is permitted to the course. Only the admission done through the proper counselling process will be entertained. The whole admission is broken down into a step-by-step process for you below.
Step 1: Appear and qualify for the NEET-UG examination of the concluding year.
Step 2: Visit the official website of Dr. NTR University of Health Science and fill out the application form with accurate details about personal and academic information.

Step 3: Submitting the application form will generate a registration number. The registration number will be sent to your registered mobile number or email. (Registration Fees for UR/OBS category are INR 2950/- (2500+450(GST@18%)), and for SC/ST category are INR 2360/- (2000/-+340(GST@18%)).
Step 4: Participate in the counselling session conducted by the counselling authority. The final allotment list will be published on their official website.
Step 5: The candidates who are on the list must report to the college and complete verification of documents. Carry all of your relevant documents, both in originals and photocopies.
Step 6: Lastly, you need to confirm your seat allotment to the allotted college by paying the prescribed fees.

Remember, applying for the BAMS admission in Andhra Pradesh does not guarantee your seats. If false or inaccurate information is found on the application form, the counselling authority can cancel the candidature at any time.

sections.heading: Documents Required for Admission

content.text: The BAMS admission in Andhra Pradesh requires a list of documents at the time of application and the verification procedure. The documents are prescribed as per the counselling authority, Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences.

items: NEET UG Rank Card (Mandatory)
NEET UG Admit Card (Mandatory)

Qualifying Exam Certificate (Intermediate Marks Memo OR Equivalent – Grade Certificate not Accepted) (Mandatory)
Study Certificate from sixth to Intermediate (VI to XII).
Caste Certificate (If applicable)
Income Certificate (If applicable)
Discontinuation Bond ( Rs. 100/- Non Judicial Stamp Paper ).
PwD Certificate (If applicable)
Aadhar Card
Candidate’s Latest passport-size Photo
Specimen Signature of the Candidate

content.text: Keep 05 sets of photocopies of each document mentioned above.

content.text: BAMS fees in Andhra Pradesh are low compared to those in other states of India. Here, the course fees are collected in instalments at the start of each year. The details of the fees are given below.

sections.heading: BAMS Careers in Andhra Pradesh

content.text: BAMS offers a wide range of career opportunities. Students who complete this degree from Andhra Pradesh BAMS colleges get jobs in different hospitals and nursing homes. Some of the BAMS jobs in Andhra Pradesh are as Ayurvedic Doctors, Medical Officers, Consultant Doctors, Ayurveda Therapists, and Medical Writers in the government and private sectors. Manasa Ayurvedic Research Centre features Ayurvedic doctor jobs in the state. Additionally, BAMS graduates can explore opportunities in areas like medical tourism, academics, and the pharmaceutical industry.

Most colleges in the state, such as Dr. NR Shastry, the Govt. Ayurvedic College has a 100% placement record in the previous years. Their career guidance helps the students with their choice of career. Andhra Pradesh also offers colleges with PG courses, if the BAMS graduates want to pursue higher and advanced studies.

sections.heading: Conclusion

content.text: As NEET is necessary for BAMS admission in Andhra Pradesh, students must score a minimum mark in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test. Admission to the course in all the colleges in Andhra Pradesh is only through the AP Ayush Counselling conducted by the Dr NTR University of Health Sciences. The state has a total of 3 colleges for BAMS with a very affordable fee structure.

sections.heading: BAMS Admission Process in Gujarat

content.text: The whole procedure of BAMS admission in Gujarat is given below in a step-by-step guide to help students navigate smoothly through the admission process.
Step 1: Appear and score above the cut-off marks in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test. The Gujarat Ayurved University sets the cut-off each year.
Step 2: Fill out the application form to apply for the AYUSH state counselling session conducted by the ACPUGMEC .
Step 3: The whole counselling process occurs online through their centralised portal. Register yourself on it with all the necessary documents and generate your login credentials.
Step 4: During the counselling session, the next step is to provide your college preferences. Select colleges according to your preference in the choice filling round.

Step 7: Lastly, to finalise your candidature, pay the prescribed admission fees to confirm your admission to the college.

Remember, there happens to be 4 rounds of counselling for BAMS admission in Gujarat – Round 1, Round 2, the Mop-Up Round, and the Stray Vacancy Round. If your seat is not allotted in a round, you can participate in the further rounds.

This course moulds the students to get a hands-on experience in Ayurveda. There are a total of 32 BAMS colleges in Gujarat. Among them, 8 are government colleges and 24 are private ones. BAMS Admission in Gujarat 2025 Overview

All of the aspirants who want to pursue the BAMS undergrad degree must appear for the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET UG) and qualify it. NEET-UG qualified candidates can only attend the AYUSH state counselling. The Gujarat Ayush Counselling session is conducted by the Admission Committee for Professional Undergraduate Medical Courses (ACPUGMEC). All over the country, the procedure for BAMS admission is the same. There are 2392 total BAMS seats in Gujarat. All these seats are distributed in 32 private and government colleges equally. The state council regulates the whole BAMS admission in Gujarat. While the NEET is mandatory for BAMS admission, candidates also have to complete their 12th with PCB (Physics, Chemistry, and Biology) subjects.

BAMS Admission Process in Gujarat

The whole procedure of BAMS admission in Gujarat is given below in a step-by-step guide to help students navigate smoothly through the admission process.

Step 1: Appear and score above the cut-off marks in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test. The Gujarat Ayurved University sets the cut-off each year.

Step 2: Fill out the application form to apply for the AYUSH state counselling session conducted by the ACPUGMEC .

Step 3: The whole counselling process occurs online through their centralised portal. Register yourself on it with all the necessary documents and generate your login credentials.

Step 4: During the counselling session, the next step is to provide your college preferences. Select colleges according to your preference in the choice filling round.

Step 5: Based on the candidate’s NEET score and state rank, the counselling authority will allot seats. The allotment list is published, depending on your preferences and seat availability in the college.

Step 6: Once your seat is allotted, report to your college with all the documents, both in originals and photocopies, and complete the document verification.

Step 7: Lastly, to finalise your candidature, pay the prescribed admission fees to confirm your admission to the college.

Remember, there happens to be 4 rounds of counselling for BAMS admission in Gujarat – Round 1, Round 2, the Mop-Up Round, and the Stray Vacancy Round. If your seat is not allotted in a round, you can participate in the further rounds.

BAMS Eligibility in Gujarat

The aspirants must consider the following set of eligibility criteria before taking BAMS admission in Gujarat. The BAMS eligibility in Gujarat includes a qualifying entrance exam.

Academic Qualification

Candidates must pass their 12th board exam with subjects Physics, Chemistry, and Biology (PCB subjects).

Candidates need to secure a 50% aggregate in their board exam in PCB subjects. (For SC/ST candidates, the aggregate is 40%)

Entrance Exam

Candidates must qualify NEET UG 2025 exam with a high percentile, which is higher than the cut-off mark set by the Gujarat Ayurved University.

Age Limit

The willing students need to be over 17 years of age on 31st December, 2025.

Documents Required for Admission

The set of documents required for BAMS admission in Gujarat is pre-prescribed by the ACPUGMEC. Remember to carry them both in originals and photocopies. Failing to produce any single one of them at the time of document verification may result in the cancellation of the candidature. The list is given below.

Admit card of NEET UG

Result / Rank Letter of NEET UG

Allotment Letter

12th Mark Statement

School Leaving / Transfer Certificate / Migration

Proof of Date of Birth (10th Passing Certificate / Birth Certificate)

Proof of Identity (Self-Attested Photocopy of Aadhar Card / Voter Card / PAN Card / Driving License)

Proof of Address (Self-Attested Photocopy of Domicile Certificate / Passport of the Candidate)

Physical / Medical Fitness Certificate

Passport size Photographs (6 copies)

Self-Attested Photocopy of Caste Certificate /Non-Creamy Layer/ Disability Certificate (if applicable)

BAMS Fees in Gujarat

BAMS fees in Gujarat are set by the college in which you are taking admission. As the Government of India and the Ministry of AYUSH jointly agreed to give the colleges independence to set their own admission fees for BAMS.

Also, the BAMS fees in Gujarat are different in government and private colleges. While the government ones take lower fees, the private ones promise flourishing infrastructure and well-trained faculty with higher fees. For a more detailed fee structure, visit the official website of the college.

BAMS Opportunities in Gujarat

BAMS graduates have diverse career options. The passouts of the previous years have secured BAMS jobs in Gujarat in several posts like Medical Officer, Ayurvedic Doctor, Research and Academics, Pharmaceutical Industrials, etc. Many hospitals and nursing homes are on the lookout for BAMS graduates. The demand for Ayurveda is increasing day by day, and with it, the job opportunities are skyrocketing in India. The average BAMS salary in Gujarat is INR 4 – 6 Lakhs annually. But the BAMS doctor salary in Gujarat is more. BAMS graduates can also pursue further studies in different specialisations of Ayurveda.

There are 3024 BAMS vacancy in Gujarat – 429 government seats and 2595 private seats. All these seats are also divided into state quota and all-India quota. BAMS Admission in Kerala Overview

It is mandatory to qualify for NEET-UG and participate in Ayush counselling for admission to the BAMS course. The Kerala AYUSH counselling is conducted by the Commissioner of Entrance Examinations (CEE) . There are a total of 1096 BAMS seats in the state. There are 5 government colleges responsible for 346 seats, and the other 13 private colleges take up 750 students. Kerala BAMS counselling happens once a year. The National Eligibility cum Entrance Test is mandatory for BAMS admission in Kerala. All the BAMS seats in Kerala are offered under both the State Quota and All India Quota. The eligibility for BAMS admission in Kerala is stated below.

Eligibility for BAMS Course in Kerala

NEET is mandatory for BAMS admission in Kerala. Apart from the qualifying exam, students must meet certain requirements for admission. The eligibility for the BAMS course in Kerala requires the students to meet the following criteria.

Securing a qualifying score in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test(NEET UG) is mandatory for BAMS admission in Kerala. NEET is a national-level entrance exam that is conducted by NTA every year.

Candidates must complete 10+2 or equivalent examination from a recognised board with Physics, Chemistry and Biology (PCB) as core subjects.

The minimum marks required for BAMS admission can vary depending on the college and reservation category. Generally, a minimum aggregate of 50% in PCB subjects is mandatory for the general category. However, some colleges might have a higher cut-off percentage. SC, ST, and OBC categories have lower mark requirements, which is 40% aggregate marks.

Candidates should be aged over 17 years at the time of admission.

BAMS Admission Process in Kerala

The step-by-step procedure for BAMS admission in Kerala is given below. All admissions, regardless to the private or government colleges, occur according to the CEE.

Step 1: Appear in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test and score above the cut-off marks for admission in the BAMS course.

Step 2: Go to the Kerala AYUSH counselling website and complete your registration. Fill out the application form by inputting all of your personal and academic information.

Step 3: Complete the document verification procedure. Carry all the prescribed documents, both in photocopies and originals.

Step 4: Take part in the Kerala State Counselling. Provide your preferences and fill choices of colleges.

Step 5: Seat allotment occurs based on NEET Ayush rank, options filled, reservation criteria, etc. You can view your seat allotment status on the counselling portal.

Step 6: Once allotted a seat, report to the college to finalise your candidature. It requires paying the admission fees necessary for confirmation.

10th Certificate (Matriculation Certificate).

content.text: A stepwise guide is given below for the students who are willing to take BAMS admission in Madhya Pradesh. It covers the whole procedure, including an overview of the counselling conducted.
Step 1: At first, appear in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET UG) conducted by the NTA. Score above the cut-off mark to have a higher chance of admission.

Step 2: Next, enrol yourself for the counselling session that is conducted by the Department of AYUSH, Government of Madhya Pradesh. Register on the official website at https://ayush.mponline.gov.in/ to generate login credentials.
Step 3: While registering, submit all of your documents and personal information. Those documents will be verified during the counselling session.

BAMS Admission Process in Madhya Pradesh

A stepwise guide is given below for the students who are willing to take BAMS admission in Madhya Pradesh. It covers the whole procedure, including an overview of the counselling conducted.

Step 1: At first, appear in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET UG) conducted by the NTA. Score above the cut-off mark to have a higher chance of admission.

After qualifying NEET UG examination, one must attend the counselling session for BAMS admission. There, the students are allotted their seats at the college based on their NEET rank, choice of colleges, and reservation. Out of 8 colleges, there is only one Government college, and the others are private ones. In total, 430 seats are available for BAMS admission in Tamil Nadu, and the Government college has 60 seats. BAMS Eligibility in Tamil Nadu

The eligibility criteria for the BAMS course are the same throughout India. The eligibility for BAMS admission in Tamil Nadu is as follows.

Students must appear in the NEET-UG examination and qualify with a minimum cutoff score.

Aspirants must have cleared Class 12 from a recognised board with subjects – Physics, Chemistry & Biology.

Students should have obtained a minimum percentage of 50% marks in the PCB subjects. For ST/SC and other reserved candidates, the minimum aggregate is 40%.

Students should be aged 17 years and above at the time of admission.

BAMS Admission Process in Tamil Nadu

The BAMS admission in Tamil Nadu is lengthy. Here we have provided a step-by-step guide for you. Follow these steps to complete the process successfully.

Step 1: First, appear in the NEET UG examination and score above the cut-off marks of that year to become eligible for BAMS admission.

Step 2: Register yourself on the Tamil Nadu state AYUSH counselling portal. The Directorate of Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy conducts the state counselling of Tamil Nadu.

Step 3: Upload and submit the necessary documents for admission. Upon submitting, a confirmation email will be sent to be registered email address.

Step 4: Attend the counselling, make your choice of the preferred colleges, and lock your choices.

Step 5: Depending on the NEET rank, candidates will be allotted BAMS seats according to their choices and seat availability in the colleges.

Step 6: Students must report to the colleges they are allotted. Remember to carry the required documents, both in originals and photocopies, and complete your document verification.

NEET Hall ticket

NEET Score Card

10th Marksheet & Certificate
